t: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference I
o: Find any pair (i, j) with |i−j| ≥ indexDifference and |nums[i]−nums[j]| ≥ valueDifference. Note i may equal j (both differences become 0). With n ≤ 100 even brute force passes, but a prefix-min/max scan gives O(n) and scales.
k: For fixed j, any earlier index within range works if nums[j] differs enough from the running min OR max of candidates.
Maintaining prefix min and max lets us test each j in O(1).

a.i: Try all ordered pairs (i, j); return the first satisfying both conditions. Trivially correct and fast enough for n ≤ 100.
s: Double loop over i and j.
Return [i,j] when both absolute conditions hold.
a.t: O(n²) — all pairs examined in the worst case

a.i: Sweep j left to right keeping the min and max of nums[0..j−indexDifference]. If nums[j] exceeds max by valueDifference or falls below min by it, that stored index pairs with j. Each j is checked once against two extremes, which is sufficient because only extremes can achieve a large gap.
s: Iterate j from indexDifference to n-1.
Before checking j, incorporate index j−indexDifference into running min/max (with their indices).
If nums[j] − maxVal ≥ vd return [maxIdx, j]; if minVal − nums[j] ≥ vd return [minIdx, j].

c.python:
class Solution:
    def findIndices(self, nums, indexDifference, valueDifference):
        n = len(nums)
        mn = mx = nums[0]; mni = mxi = 0
        for j in range(indexDifference, n):
            i = j - indexDifference
            if nums[i] < mn: mn, mni = nums[i], i
            if nums[i] > mx: mx, mxi = nums[i], i
            if nums[j] - mx >= valueDifference: return [mxi, j]
            if mn - nums[j] >= valueDifference: return [mni, j]
        return [-1, -1]

a.t: O(n) — single pass with constant work per index

w: Brute force is acceptable here, but present the prefix-min/max idea to show scalability (it solves the harder version with n up to 10^5). Edge cases: indexDifference 0 allows i = j; watch for empty candidate windows when j < indexDifference.
